title: Nasruddin Tale 200: The Locked Gate with No Walls
summary: In his final years in the town of Aksehir, Mulla Nasruddin designed his own tomb....
full_text:
In his final years in the town of Aksehir, Mulla Nasruddin designed his own tomb.

He built a magnificent iron gate, fitted with a gigantic, heavy brass padlock that could never be opened. But around the gate, there were no walls, no fences, and no barriers whatsoever—the open green fields stretched freely on every side!

Travelers came from across the world and asked in bewilderment: "Why is there an enormous locked gate with no walls? Anyone can simply walk around it!"

Nasruddin's ghost chuckled from the eternal meadows: "That is the supreme riddle of human existence! Mortals spend their lives beating their heads against locked gates of dogma, fear, and pride, blind to the fact that the walls never existed, and that freedom and truth surround them on every side!"
moral: The gates of illusion are locked with heavy padlocks, yet the walls never existed at all.
